**Exceptions are limited and explained.** Each entry of `fidelity-exceptions.json` has `role`, `name`, `category`, `reason`, `approved_by` (`"builder proposal, pending design engineer"` until confirmed) and maps to a Conflicts item; none covers a value the data can supply (a count, a label, a status, a cite). — verify: file content; build.md maps each to a Conflicts number.

**Default state from data.** `/work/W-2201` shows the title, subtitle, agent-note lines, the saved parts with cites, the five records groups with their returned counts text, and the two step buttons, all from the fixture; a field the fixture omits draws nothing. — verify: `tests/weekly.test.tsx`; page at 1440 and 390.

**The form carries the PM's words.** Pressing "Send to Tola to assemble" opens a form with four labelled text areas and four cite pickers showing the saved values; the cite picker offers only the records E-LINE-OPTIONS returns for `weekly_report`; no control writes, suggests or generates text. — verify: component test with a recording `fetch`; a search of `features/workspace/**` and fixtures shows no generate/suggest control for these parts.

**Write request.** Submitting sends exactly one POST `/api/v1/work/W-2201/steps` with CSRF, `expected_revision` = `workspace.revision`, `step: "send_to_tola"`, `inputs` with the eight names (cites as lists of option values) and a UUID `idempotency_key`; no `note`, no `evidence_ids`; the body validates against the generated request schema. **Nothing is judged client-side.** Typing "TBD" or leaving a cite empty sends the request as is; the page shows only the server's answer. — verify: component test (request recorded; no local message).

**422 per part.** On W-2202 pressing Send shows the server message under `risks` and under `next_steps_cites` (`aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`), the top `message` above the form, focus on the first failing input, inputs kept, and a new key for the next press. **Send moves to assembling.** A `done` on W-2201 `send_to_tola` reloads once and the page shows the assembling state (W-2203): the agent name, step text, three progress lines with their statuses as words, "TEST TEMPLATE", and the disabled "Send for PMO Lead review" with its reason; activating it sends nothing. — verify: component test and e2e with the recorded requests.

**Assembling is quiet and accessible.** The `now` item pulses only without `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`; its state reads as a word; no step on W-2203 is actionable. — verify: e2e with `reducedMotion: 'reduce'` (no running animation on the `now` mark) and a component test for `aria-disabled`.

risk.rationale: Medium. The work is on a shared renderer (`features/work-item/**`, touched by F-09, F-14, F-16, F-17) and a proposed v7 contract (D-LINE-WORKSPACE) that the backend may change. The review state includes "Approve and send", which sends to a client (INV-RESEND, effect_uncertain). It stays at medium because all of it is on the mock, the send is unimplemented in the backend, and nothing is released. SURFACES: ui (8 boards), api (E-WORK-STEP, E-WORK-ITEM workspace), contract-change (proposed block), external-messaging (client report send and uncertain-effect handling). PRODUCT-ACCEPTANCE is not-required because the work conforms to the client-approved boards. The business rules (four cited parts, PMO Lead review, exact version sent) are already on the boards and in screens.md.

Saved cites are lost when the form opens. On W-2201 the four text areas prefill with the saved words, but all four "Cites for ..." pickers open empty. Pressing "Save draft" or "Send to Tola to assemble" then sends no `*_cites` at all (I recorded the W-2202 request: `inputs` holds only status, risks, timeline, next_steps). A PM who saved cited parts would silently erase the cites, and Send would draw a "cite at least one record" 422 for parts that were already cited. Spec AC 7 says the form shows "the saved values" for the cites too, and the page's own "Your update" text shows them as cited. build.md names this as a contract limit (records `value` is a string), but the fixture/mock path can still carry the cites (or the form must not offer a Save that drops them). Fix it in the frame (prefill from the item's saved cites) or put a visible line in the form saying the cites are kept, and record the decision. Without that, the journey "write four cited parts, send" is not usable.

findings.summary: Carried forward from SEC-5-C1 (F-17), not a defect in this diff. The frontend lock is a UI safeguard only. It cannot stop a second tab, a stale tab, a direct API call or another client. The real guard against a duplicate client email is server-side, and it is not built. It must be built and tested before any real weekly send is enabled. What the server must do is in Notes 1 to 3.

A cited record goes into a report that is sent outside PSL. The frontend only offers values that E-LINE-OPTIONS returns (`RecordPicker`), but a direct call to E-WORK-STEP can send any string in `inputs.*_cites`. Expected: on `send_to_tola` and `save_draft`, the server checks that every cited value is in the set the actor is allowed to see for this case and week. It answers 422 on the named field otherwise and never resolves a citation it did not authorise. E-LINE-OPTIONS must also be scoped to the actor, the tenant and this item's case. Today the mock hook (`frontend/mock/start-work.mjs:23-25,110-112`) is keyed by line and persona only, which is acceptable for a mock.

The omitted-cites behaviour is safe on the frontend. The frame sends no `*_cites` key and no empty list when untouched, and the new test pins both. The hint "saved cites stay" is a server claim (omitted = keep) that the backend must confirm. Send on a saved draft without re-picking cites still returns 422 until `records` fields can prefill. This is the builder's own contract question for the coordinator, not a blocker.

`data-form-open` is set only while a `ws:` form is open, and the form renders in the aside outside the Decide panel (Workspace.tsx:324). So `display:none` cannot hide the form. The form has its own submit and close, and a reconcile step uses the same `ws:` path, so no action or reconcile path is lost. Closing re-shows the bar, and the focus-return runs in rAF after the state change. The rule applies only in the phone media block. The bar's own "confirm first" hint is not shown while the form is open, which is acceptable.

The cite hint promises server behaviour that is unconfirmed, and contradicts the Send 422. Decision: it is not honest as worded, and the empty pickers beside it leave the PM unable to tell what is saved. I would accept a hint that promises nothing about the server and tells the PM what to do on this page, on all eight cite fields (W-2201 has two sets): "Saved records are not shown here. Choose at least one record for this part before you send." Also acceptable: drop the hint and keep the existing "Your update" section above, which already lists the saved cites, plus a single line under the form heading with the same sentence. Do not say "stay on it" or "kept" until the backend confirms that omitted cites are kept on Save draft and counted on Send; if the backend confirms both, the original sentence is then fine and Send on a saved draft no longer 422s. Update the hint test to assert the new sentence. Also record the list-valued `records` `value` contract question for the coordinator as the real fix (prefill), so the hint can be removed later.
